topic: Lorach soft particle Hermite depth-fade vs hard Z-test billboard terrain clipping seam rig
topic_zh: Lorach 软粒子三阶埃尔米特深度消隐（DepthFade）对比朴素硬件 Z 测试广告牌插地硬切痕
scope: Deterministic Tristan Lorach (NVIDIA GPU Gems 3, 2007) cubic Hermite soft particle depth-fade (alpha_soft = alpha_0 * s^2 * (3 - 2s), s = clamp((z_scene - z_particle)/d_fade, 0, 1)) versus naive hardware Z-test billboard clipping and 64-slab volumetric parabolic density quadrature across 17 depth-clearance stations (Delta_z in [-0.40m, +1.20m]). No neural volumetric splatting execution.

protocol.function: α_soft = α₀ · s²(3 − 2s) where s = clamp(Δz / d_fade, 0, 1) → α(+0.20m) = 0.1250 (0.0000 Cardboard Seam)

robustness.name: Sampled 17 depth-clearance stations feather particle intersections with C1 continuity and zero cardboard seams

good_fit: Ground-hugging smoke, explosion fireballs, waterfall mist, dust clouds, and shockwave billboards in UE5, Unity, and Three.js
Eliminating razor-sharp 2D polygon intersection lines where billboard quads slice into sloped terrain or walls
Guaranteeing C1 zero-derivative opacity contact at Δz = 0 and Δz = d_fade via cubic Hermite s²(3 − 2s)
Replacing 64-step per-particle volumetric ray marching with a 1-tap scene depth buffer lookup
not_for: Opaque rigid debris particles (rocks, shrapnel, shell casings) that should intersect or collide sharply
Pure forward pipelines without a readable depth texture / depth prepass
Neural 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) or NeRF training
Camera near-plane clipping (requires separate near-plane distance fade)
